bubbleNote.blurb: Alabama is the first team out at the 13 seed, one spot from the field. The Tide are close enough that a single result above them could do the work for them.
LSU sits 14th, two spots off the field, and gets an immediate opportunity: No. 23 Clemson comes to Baton Rouge next. Win that and the bubble talk gets a lot quieter.
USC holds the 15 seed, three spots from the field. The Trojans need help and results, in that order.
BYU is the last team on the bubble at No. 16, four spots from the field. With the Big 12 auto bid still in play, the path exists -- it's just narrow.

games.blurb: A top-25 opener in Baton Rouge, and the oddsmakers aren't treating it like a coin flip: No. 13 LSU is a 10.5-point favorite over No. 23 Clemson with the total sitting at a modest 50.5. Points may be at a premium in a game that could shape both playoff cases in September.
The Apple Cup is back on the Week 1 slate, but not as a toss-up: No. 19 Washington is favored by 21.5 at home. Washington State's job is to make the rivalry feel like one again.

Louisville heads to Oxford as a 6.5-point underdog against No. 10 Ole Miss, the tightest spread on any ranked-team opener here. With a total of 55.5, expect this one to be decided by whoever gets the last possession.

No. 5 Notre Dame opens with a 20.5-point cushion over Wisconsin and a total of just 47.5 -- the market sees a grinder that the Irish still control. Style points matter for a team with playoff ambitions and no conference title to fall back on.
The Border War kicks off the weekend with Colorado State favored by just four at home. Neither side is ranked, but four points between rivals means bragging rights are genuinely up for grabs.
No. 16 Michigan is a 26.5-point favorite over Western Michigan in the Big House. This is a tune-up, and the only real question is how quickly the Wolverines put it away.

predictions.blurb: Texas sits fourth in the poll while FPI slots the Longhorns at No. 2 -- the metrics think this SEC contender is being underrated at the top of the board.
Texas Tech checks in at No. 12 with FPI a touch higher at No. 10, a rare case of poll and computer broadly agreeing on the Big 12 favorite.
Michigan is No. 16 in the poll and No. 15 in FPI. Nobody's arguing about the Wolverines' place in the Big Ten pecking order just yet.
BYU is the poll's No. 15 team but only 20th by FPI, the widest disconnect in this group. The Cougars will need results to settle the argument.
LSU ranks 13th in the poll and ninth in FPI, and a Week 1 date with Clemson is a fast chance to prove the computers right.

fieldStorylines.blurb: The Big Ten's automatic bid is a two-team argument: No. 1 Ohio State and No. 2 Oregon are separated by a single spot in the field. There's no margin for either one.
Georgia holds the SEC's auto bid at No. 3 with Texas breathing down its neck at No. 4. One slip from the Bulldogs flips the league's playoff pecking order.
Texas Tech leads the Big 12 at No. 12 with BYU three spots back at No. 15 -- the widest leader-chaser gap among the power leagues, but hardly a settled race.
